_comment: Worked examples for the Ticket view journey checker. Each one is a journey the campaign has something to say about, so the checker opens on a real case instead of an empty form. `from`/`to` are NaPTAN ATCO codes and are checked against data/timetable.sqlite by pytest — a preset pointing at a stop that is not in the timetable would fail silently at runtime.

presets.label: Lancing → Brighton
presets.note: One bus, across the DayRider zone boundary
presets.why: A direct 700 from Lancing seafront, the stop on the Coastliner closest to the town centre. Like the Worthing journey it crosses the Worthing/Brighton DayRider boundary, so no single zone ticket covers it and the checker's answer has the same shape. It used to start at Lancing Station, which the 700 does not serve, and came back as two buses.

presets.label: Worthing → Brighton
presets.why: A direct Coastliner run that still crosses the Worthing/Brighton DayRider boundary, so no single zone ticket covers it.

presets.label: Shoreham → Universities
presets.why:
Shoreham High Street to the Brighton University stop on Lewes Road, which is where the buses students actually take go: the 25 and the 3X both call here, and both are Brighton & Hove.

It used to point at Park Road in Coldean, which was wrong in a way the fare answer hid. Park Road is served by the 5B and the N25, not by the 25 or the 3X, so the only itinerary the checker could build ran a Stagecoach 700 and then a Brighton & Hove 5B — two operators, and a reader would reasonably conclude two tickets. The journey people make is a 2 into the centre and a 25 out along Lewes Road, both Brighton & Hove, both inside citySAVER, one ticket.

The change is a short walk across the Old Steine interchange rather than a stop-for-stop one: the 2 sets down at North Street or St James's Street and the 25 leaves from Royal Pavilion, about ninety metres away. That is what a passenger does, and it is why the two services can look unconnected to a search that matches only identical stops.

Labelled Universities rather than named for one campus: this stop is the University of Brighton at Moulsecoomb, with the University of Sussex at Falmer further out and halls and faculty buildings scattered along the corridor between them. Falmer is outside this dataset — the ingest keeps stops west of longitude -0.10 and Falmer is at -0.087 — but the fare picture is the same either way, because the Adur/Brighton & Hove boundary is crossed long before any campus.

presets.label: Southwick → Hole in the Wall
presets.note: Two miles, one change and a walk
presets.why: Southwick Square up to the top of Mile Oak — the full length of the route rather than the halfway point at Mile Oak Gardens, so the line on the map shows where the service actually ends. Both ends are Brighton & Hove; the interest here is how far a single operator's network reaches west of the city.

presets.label: Worthing → Hangleton
presets.why: One of the corridors with no simple route: a change, two operators, and no express option across the boundary.

presets.label: Sompting → Brighton Marina
presets.note: The long way along the coast
presets.why: End to end along the coast, from a Sompting housing estate to the Marina — about as far as this corridor goes in one trip. Sompting is Stagecoach and Compass territory; the Marina is Brighton & Hove's. It is the clearest case of a journey no single operator's ticket covers.
